THE EXPLORER’S FIELD GUIDE

A new way to see
familiar history.

Each stop is a real, dated event. Read the green side for an opportunity or helpful response, and the coral side for damage, trade-offs or risks.

Terrain & colourArt-directed metaphors for each chapter. Volcanoes, lava, ash and storm skies are visual metaphors, not records of actual eruptions. Planets, rings and satellite orbits are illustrative, not calculated prices, returns, VIX or correlations. The three moons represent opportunity, pressure and uncertainty.
Historical sourcesEach chapter links to its primary source. Interpretations are identified separately from reported facts.
Explore your wayScroll, use the dated timeline, or press the up/down buttons. Play visits each chapter for 10 seconds. Drag the planet to rotate it, or focus it and use the arrow keys. Use the +/− buttons to zoom. Enter any date to find the nearest of seven sourced chapters; dates between chapters do not have daily market data.
Planet shaderAdapted from Julien Sulpis’ realtime planet shader: procedural terrain, clouds, ocean light and atmosphere. GPL-3.0 licence · Download source. Supplied without warranty.
Planet3D creditBrowser adaptation of Ishan Oshada’s Planet3D. Its planet, moon and orbit model drives the satellites. MIT licence.
Volcanic terrainCrater and slope shaping adapted from Jaysmito Mukherjee’s TerraForge3D. Browser shader port with ash, lava and ejected fragments. MIT licence.

Prototype scope: seven curated moments from 2007–2023. No live prices or AI-generated explanations. The next stage in the project brief is connecting the world to weekly market data.
